evidence.claim: Swift Trail ends at Riggs Flat Lake, an 11-acre lake set in alpine forest and meadow high in the Pinaleños.
evidence.quote: Riggs Flat Lake is located at the end of Swift Trail, a road that winds along the top of the Pinaleño Mountains. It is a small picturesque lake, 11 acres in size, set in alpine forest and meadow.

evidence.claim: Brown and rainbow trout are stocked in the cold water during summer.

evidence.claim: West Peak is visible from the lake’s vicinity, while a short hike to an overlook gives views west to Aravaipa Valley and the Galiuro Mountains.
evidence.quote: West Peak is visible from the vicinity of the lake. So are Aravaipa Valley and the Galiuro Mountains to the west if you don't mind taking a short hike to get to an overlook.

evidence.claim: Vehicle access closes November 15 to April 15; early or late snow may extend the closure. Vehicles including trailers longer than 22 feet are not recommended on the switchbacks.
evidence.quote: Vehicles (including trailers) longer than 22 feet are not recommended because of the difficulty of negotiating the switchbacks on AZ 366. This area is not accessible by vehicle from November 15 to April 15 when the Swift Trail is closed for the winter. Early or late snow may extend the inaccessible season.

evidence.claim: These mountains are called Sky Islands because desert separates their high forests from neighboring ranges. The Pinaleños are the highest of southeastern Arizona’s Sky Islands.
evidence.quote: The mountain ranges of southeastern Arizona have come to be called Sky Islands because they are surrounded by desert and isolated from one another by seas of arid environment, so different from the tall forests that grace their upper slopes. Of all the Sky Islands in southeastern Arizona, the Pinaleños are the highest
